Two seed beats now union only when they share **two distinct link signals**.\n\n- **Strong signals** (each shared file, distinctive intent identifier, or command gram) and **weak** reinforcement (a shared recurring intent noun). Merge when there are two strong signals, or one strong reinforced by one weak.\n- **A single shared file is never enough.** A name that is only the stem of a file the pair already shares is dropped, but an identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it equals that stem — so a feature's *file AND identifier* stays merged (the `WIDGET_BETA` case).\n- **Round-2 protections kept and generalised:** project-scoped links, document-frequency pruning now applied to file/name/gram/content tokens, synthetic-turn filtering, non-stopword names. The parser (`parse.mjs`) treats `touch` as recon NOISE and records no command, so those beats reach `threads.mjs` with no files/commands/identifiers and never become seeds — the corpus yields zero threads regardless of clustering logic. I confirmed by reverting to the original single-link engine that this gate fails **identically** (\"found 0\") before my change, so it is not a regression. Making it pass requires the parser to surface `touch` paths — a parser-behaviour change requiring a `PARSER_VERSION` bump, which the spec explicitly forbids and scopes outside `threads.mjs`.
